rationale: The Parkinson diet cohort recorded mango without measuring fatigue severity. The mixed smoothie comparison was inconclusive and only some flavors contained mango. A pulp trial reported biomarkers. The bark-and-flower blend changed some exercise performance measures in healthy men but measured no validated subjective fatigue. The raw-fruit claim remains open.

Corn-oil studies use a shared carrier, mixed or topical formulations, or tests outside Parkinson disease. Overnight polysomnography in healthy people gave inconclusive comparisons and used corn oil in both arms. Topical postherpetic neuralgia treatment measured global sleep quality. The adolescent protocol gives no verified sleep results. No rated Parkinson insomnia comparison isolates refined corn oil.
